query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Introducing approximately 5 at.% aluminum (Al) into equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr via vacuum arc melting will enhance the alloy’s oxygen resistance at high temperatures by promoting the in-situ formation of a continuous, protective alumina (Al₂O₃) scale on the surface, while maintaining its inherent tensile ductility and high-temperature yield strength.
generation.material_initial_state: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloy exhibiting 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C under strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹, but with poor oxygen resistance.
generation.intervention: Alloying with approximately 5 at.% aluminum (Al) using vacuum arc melting to incorporate Al homogeneously into the bulk alloy.
generation.conditions: High-temperature oxidation in air at 1000 °C for exposure times up to 100 hours; mechanical performance (tensile ductility at room temperature and yield strength at 1000 °C) evaluated under strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹.
generation.structural_mediator: Formation of a thin (∼1–2 μm), continuous and adherent Al₂O₃ layer at the alloy surface during high-temperature exposure.
generation.mechanism: Reactive Al preferentially oxidizes during high-temperature exposure to form a stable, slow-growing alumina scale that acts as a barrier to further oxygen diffusion into the alloy, thereby preserving the bulk microstructure and mechanical properties.
generation.predicted_outcome: Compared to untreated HfNbTaTiZr, the Al-alloyed material will display significantly reduced oxygen uptake and oxidation penetration while retaining similar tensile ductility (8–16%) and high-temperature yield strength (163–530 MPa).
generation.baseline: Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr with poor oxygen resistance under identical high-temperature oxidation conditions.
generation.boundary: Effective for exposures at 1000 °C in air up to ~100 hours and under mechanical loading at strain rates between 10⁻⁴ and 10⁻² s⁻¹; the intervention should not result in formation of deleterious intermetallic compounds or deteriorate the single-phase BCC microstructure.
generation.uncertainty: The optimal Al concentration may require fine-tuning to balance oxide scale formation without compromising the alloy’s phase stability or ductility. It is also uncertain whether the alumina scale will remain adherent over prolonged cyclic oxidation or thermal cycling conditions.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two sets of specimens: one group of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr with ~5 at.% Al and a control group without Al addition, produced under identical vacuum arc melting conditions. Expose both groups to high-temperature oxidation in air at 1000 °C for 100 hours. Post-exposure, perform cross-sectional microscopy (e.g., SEM/EDS) to evaluate oxide scale continuity and thickness, and conduct mechanical tests (room-temperature tensile and high-temperature yield tests at 1000 °C under 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹ strain rates).
measurements: Oxide scale thickness and uniformity via microscopy and elemental mapping
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the Al-alloyed specimens do not show a significantly thinner, more uniform protective alumina scale (and correspondingly lower weight gain and oxygen penetration) compared to the control, or if they exhibit a statistically significant degradation in tensile ductility or high-temperature yield strength relative to the baseline, then the hypothesis is rejected.
